verdict_inference_sentence.value: The 95% block-bootstrap interval for the RMSE ratio (0.780 to 1.335) contains 1, and the Diebold–Mariano test (HLN-corrected) gives p = 0.961, so on 18 holdout decisions the model cannot be distinguished from Always Hold in either direction.

source.method: src.app.verdict_inference_sentence

rps_supplementary_sentence.value: Supplementary measure (exploratory, added after the holdout had been seen; the pre-specified verdict stays RMSE-based): the ranked probability score on the same holdout (lower is better) is 0.154 for the model, 0.194 for Always Hold and 0.159 for the class frequencies of the estimation sample. Simple class frequencies do almost as well as the model, so the six factors add little beyond the base rates of cuts, holds and hikes; most of the gain over Always Hold comes from admitting that cuts and hikes happen.

policy_inertia_sentence.value: Policy-inertia specifications (exploratory only; P0 = inflation, its 3-month change, the ex-post real rate and the previous decision; P1 = P0 plus the other five factors, ridge). RPS of the specification vs the main model M0 — P0: rolling origin inside the estimation sample 0.165 vs 0.213; fixed-origin holdout 0.220 vs 0.154; recursive holdout 0.156 vs 0.148 | P1: rolling origin inside the estimation sample 0.173 vs 0.213; fixed-origin holdout 0.254 vs 0.154; recursive holdout 0.144 vs 0.148. P0 has the lower RPS in 1 of 3 designs; P1 has the lower RPS in 2 of 3 designs. The ranking depends on the evaluation design, which is instability, not an improvement; neither specification replaces the pre-specified model.

holdout_update_sentence.value: Interpretation of the data update: the holdout is the last 18 usable decisions (2024-09-02 to 2026-10-27); appending a decision moves the unchanged chronological split rule, so the estimation and holdout windows shift with the data. 1 of these decisions (2026-10-27) took place after the specification was dated (2026-10-16); the other 17 had already been seen in earlier runs. The holdout is therefore partly newer data but still not an untouched confirmatory holdout.

version_change_sentence.value: Effect of the data update (OLD = git tag before-data-update-2026-09-07, NEW = current files): usable decisions 88 → 89; estimation sample 70 → 71 decisions (ending 2024-06-03 → 2024-07-15); holdout 18 → 18 decisions (2024-07-15–2026-09-07 → 2024-09-02–2026-10-27). The holdout RMSE ratio changed from 1.002 to 0.995, so the pre-specified rule's label changed from "does not meet the pre-specified criterion (RMSE ratio not below 1)" to "meets the pre-specified criterion (RMSE ratio below 1)". 95% bootstrap intervals: OLD 0.828 to 1.230, NEW 0.780 to 1.335; both ratios lie inside both intervals, so the change does not show that the model forecasts better or worse than before.
